questions.question: Simplify the reasons for using VPN in companies.
questions.solution_html:
• Simplify the reasons for using VPN in companies.
  • • Secure Remote Access: Allows employees to connect safely to the company's internal private network from any
  • location via the public internet.
  • • Data Confidentiality & Cost Savings: Encrypts sensitive corporate data streams securely, replacing the need for highly
  • expensive physical leased lines.
  • Initiation & Parameter Handshake: Client contacts the endpoint gateway; the nodes negotiate matching cryptographic
  • specs.
  • Credential Collection: The system collects identity tokens (passwords, PINs, certificates, or biometrics) submitted by
  • the remote endpoint client.
  • Gateway Setup & Initial Configuration: Define public interface interfaces, configure specific subnet routing rules, and
  • pool internal IP resources for remote connections.
  • Initial Permutation (IP): Incoming 64-bit plaintext blocks are systematically rearranged using a fixed structural
  • permutation matrix.
  • User Connection Request: A remote employee submits their unique enterprise corporate network credentials via their
  • edge VPN client interface.
  • Site-to-Site VPN (Gateway-to-Gateway Architecture): links permanent networks across different physical locations
  • over public internet connections. Local network routers or perimeter firewalls act as dedicated VPN gateways handling all
  • encapsulation and decryption. Example: A multinational medical enterprise connecting its primary data center in New
  • York to regional clinics across Texas using persistent, static IPsec tunnels terminated on corporate Cisco ASA firewalls.
questions.final_answer: York to regional clinics across Texas using persistent, static IPsec tunnels terminated on corporate Cisco ASA firewalls
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Define VPN protocols.
questions.solution_html:
• VPN protocols are a standardized framework of cryptographic rules, encapsulation techniques, and transmission
  • agreements (such as IPsec, SSL/TLS, PPTP, and L2TP) that dictate exactly how data is packaged, encrypted, and securely
  • tunneled over public paths.
  • Identity Evaluation & Tunneling: User parameters/certificates are validated, symmetric crypto elements are safely
  • configured, and a secure operational virtual pipeline is locked down.
  • Directory Validation & Allocation: The gateway validates submission packets against active directories (like RADIUS
  • LDAP) and returns user authorization permissions.
  • Authentication Core Integration: Bind the central edge firewall framework to corporate directory servers (LDAP
  • RADIUS) and apply multi-factor access challenges.
  • Block Division: The permuted block splits into two symmetrical 32-bit segments: Left (L ) and Right (R ).
  • 0 0
  • Gateway Relay & LDAP Bind: The VPN Gateway catches the request and opens a secure, encrypted connection
  • (typically LDAPS over TCP port 636) to the destination LDAP directory node, executing an administrative lookup bind.
  • Remote Access VPN (Client-to-Gateway Architecture): links an individual isolated computer terminal safely to a
  • secure internal enterprise backend network. Users initiate connection via a dedicated software app on their endpoint
  • which validates credentials and establishes an encrypted pipeline to the network edge firewall. Example: An accounting
  • executive working from home launching a desktop application like FortiClient or Cisco AnyConnect to log in and securely
  • access private internal payroll databases.

questions.question: Explain AES-256 preferred in VPN.
questions.solution_html:
• • High Security Tier: Employs a 256-bit cryptographic key depth, creating an exponentially massive combination field that
  • renders mathematical brute-force breaches completely impossible.
  • • Optimized Performance: Provides supreme hardware execution efficiency, delivering robust encryption defenses
  • without significantly reducing active network bandwidth speeds.
  • Endpoint Package Provisioning: Output and install preconfigured endpoint connection tools or security profiles across
  • remote terminal groups.
  • The Inner Feistel Function (f) Components
  • • Expansion (E-box): Expands the 32-bit right-hand data vector to 48 bits.
  • • Subkey Mixing (XOR): Combines the expanded 48-bit result with the round's unique 48-bit subkey.
  • • S-Box Substitution: Routes the XOR output through 8 separate Substitution blocks (S-boxes), reducing the 48-bit
  • string back to a dense 32-bit vector while introducing crucial non-linearity .
  • • Permutation (P-box): Scrambles the 32-bit S-box output to provide diffusion.
  • Profile Authorization Mapping: Upon successful verification, the LDAP engine transmits the user's explicit profile
  • metadata and security permissions (such as group strings: memberOf: CN=Finance_VPN_Group) back to the VPN
  • Gateway.

questions.question: Compare Remote Access VPNs and SSL/TLS VPNs.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare Remote Access VPNs and SSL/TLS VPNs.
  • • Remote Access VPNs (IPsec-driven): Operate at the Network layer (OSI Layer 3). They typically demand dedicated
  • endpoint software suites and assign full virtual physical interfaces to the client terminal, granting them wider network
  • infrastructure access.
  • • SSL/TLS VPNs: Function at the Application layer (OSI Layer 7). They offer a flexible, browser-centric connection model
  • requiring no dedicated software installation, limiting user interactions specifically to designated web applications rather
  • than the entire internal network.
questions.final_answer: than the entire internal network

questions.question: Discuss about encryption algorithms used in VPNs.
questions.solution_html:
• • DES (Data Encryption Standard): Legacy 64-bit symmetric structural cipher running an old 56-bit working key length.
  • Deprecated due to vulnerability to brute-force computational decoding.
  • • 3DES (Triple DES): Wraps data blocks with the standard DES structure sequentially three times. Offers stronger
  • security than DES but suffers from high latency and low computational processing efficiency.
  • • AES (Advanced Encryption Standard): The modern global standard symmetric block cipher. Highly efficient, secure
  • and performant across low-power devices. Extensively scaled inside modern VPN networks at 128, 192, and 256-bit key
  • layers.
questions.final_answer: layers

questions.question: Explain the components of RADIUS architecture.
questions.solution_html:
• • RADIUS Client / Network Access Server (NAS): The edge access control device (such as an internal corporate VPN
  • gateway) that collects user requests and bridges them over to the central AAA database.
  • • RADIUS Server: The centralized processing hub that evaluates incoming connection validation packets, checks
  • credentials, and returns authorization codes.
  • • User Profile Directory Database: The backend enterprise repository (e.g., Active Directory or LDAP environments)
  • containing specific access records, authorization rules, and group mappings.
questions.final_answer: containing specific access records, authorization rules, and group mappings

questions.question: Compare Remote Access VPNs and SSL/TLS VPNs.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare Remote Access VPNs and SSL/TLS VPNs.
  • • Remote Access VPNs (IPsec-driven): Operate at the Network layer (OSI Layer 3). They typically demand dedicated
  • endpoint software suites and assign full virtual physical interfaces to the client terminal, granting them wider network
  • infrastructure access.
  • • SSL/TLS VPNs: Function at the Application layer (OSI Layer 7). They offer a flexible, browser-centric connection model
  • requiring no dedicated software installation, limiting user interactions specifically to designated web applications rather
  • than the entire internal network.

questions.question: Discuss about encryption algorithms used in VPNs.
questions.solution_html:
• • DES (Data Encryption Standard): Legacy 64-bit symmetric structural cipher running an old 56-bit working key length.
  • Deprecated due to vulnerability to brute-force computational decoding.
  • • 3DES (Triple DES): Wraps data blocks with the standard DES structure sequentially three times. Offers stronger
  • security than DES but suffers from high latency and low computational processing efficiency.
  • • AES (Advanced Encryption Standard): The modern global standard symmetric block cipher. Highly efficient, secure
  • and performant across low-power devices. Extensively scaled inside modern VPN networks at 128, 192, and 256-bit key
  • layers.
